correctness.rationale: For SPD A and candidate direction d, η*=−(dᵀA²e)/(dᵀA²d), so the smoothed error is oblique projection P_d e=(I−d(dᵀA²)/(dᵀA²d))e. Its exact Euclidean norm is ||d|| ||A²d||/(dᵀA²d). Applying the sharp positive-definite antieigenvalue/Kantorovich extremal inequality to B=A² with eigenvalues m=λmin(A)² and M=λmax(A)² yields ||P_d|| <=(m+M)/(2√mM)=(κ²+1)/(2κ). Endpoint-eigenspace weights attain equality for A=diag(1,κ) and d=(κ,1). Independently recomputed exact rational P, singular norm and equality errors for five κ. Residual contraction is automatic in A² norm; κ>1 admits strictly increasing Euclidean error. All scope and one-dimensional exception checked.

originality.rationale: FAIL on prior implication, not mathematical correctness: the boxed extremal factor is exactly the classical sharp antieigenvalue operator-cosine law for an SPD B=A², combined with the standard norm of a codimension-one oblique projection. Preexisting operator-trigonometry literature explicitly addresses minimum-residual iterative schemes. The frozen proof itself explicitly performs this standard substitution and has no further distinct mathematical classification beyond its two-endpoint equality witness. The exact error statement is a direct corollary of this stronger prior framework without a separate nonstandard theorem.
residual_risks: General antieigenvalue theorem source full original proof was not accessed, but its standard exact formula directly implies present extremal factor.
The sharp solver-specific operational warning is useful, but under the claimed contribution it is mathematically a direct specialization of the stronger operator inequality.
